subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: When the current process owns an asynchronous exec-approvals write lock, should synchronous readers consume a process-local committed snapshot or be allowed to read the destination without serialization?
rationale: This choice defines the authorization-store consistency boundary and trades availability against reading transient policy state; tests alone cannot establish the intended security contract.

options.title: Preserve committed-state serialization
options.body: Coordinate the sync and async paths or serve the last validated committed snapshot so readers never inspect an in-progress destination write.

options.title: Accept lockless destination reads
options.body: Explicitly accept transient destination reads only with maintainer approval and proof covering atomic and copy-fallback writers across supported platforms.

recommendation.title: Preserve committed-state serialization
recommendation.body: Coordinate the sync and async paths or serve the last validated committed snapshot so readers never inspect an in-progress destination write.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to recent exec-approval security decisions and review of the host policy contract.
